writing.title: We Were Never Asking for a Revolution
writing.description: A personal essay on queer storytelling, self-censorship and the freedom to be ordinary.

image.alt: Two women flee hand in hand from a burning convent at night

sample.audience: Readers of queer literature, personal essays and cultural commentary.
sample.objective: Use the legend of Julie d’Aubigny to ask why queer love so often has to be extraordinary to be told.

extracts.label: From the published essay
extracts.text: There is something terribly romantic about a woman who would burn down a convent for the person she loves. There is something considerably less romantic about a world in which she had to.

sample.notes: I move between the convent legend and ordinary scenes from my own life. That shift gives the essay its tension and reflects the Journal’s interest in personal writing and queer literature. The burning-convent artwork carried the opening image into the social campaign.

seo.title: We Were Never Asking for a Revolution | Mollie Sambrook
seo.description: A personal essay on queer storytelling, self-censorship and the freedom to be ordinary.

writing.title: 10 Gift Ideas to Buy a Poetry Lover
writing.description: A poetry gift guide that helps readers choose a thoughtful present and discover relevant products.

image.alt: Published poetry gift guide showing a featured product and its recommendation

sample.audience: People looking for gift ideas for a poetry lover, including readers unfamiliar with the studio.
sample.objective: Give shoppers useful recommendations they can compare before deciding what to buy.

extracts.label: From the introduction
extracts.text: Poetry lovers are notoriously difficult yet wonderfully rewarding to buy for. They rarely want disposable novelties; they crave things with depth, texture, and emotional resonance. Here are ten tactile gift ideas crafted for the sentimental and the overthinkers:

sample.notes: The recovered Semrush UK research (25–26 November 2026) estimated 70 monthly searches for “poetry gifts” and 30 for “gifts for a poetry lover”, both with informational intent. The guide mixes studio products with independent recommendations. Product links give readers a next step once they recognise an idea that suits the recipient.

seo.title: 10 Gift Ideas to Buy a Poetry Lover | Mollie Sambrook
seo.description: A poetry gift guide that helps readers choose a thoughtful present and discover relevant products.

writing.title: Almost, Always
writing.description: Published product copy for a poetry journal designed around the words we almost say.

image.alt: The original Almost, Always journal covers and an open spread

sample.audience: Poetry readers, journal writers and people choosing a gift for a writer.
sample.objective: Give the journal emotional meaning and answer practical questions that matter before buying.

extracts.label: From the published product description
extracts.text:
Some things are easier to write than to speak.

Almost, Always. is a poetry-inspired hardcover journal from Cold Feet Editions, created for the thoughts that linger, the conversations we rehearse and the feelings we haven't quite found the language for.

sample.notes: The opening gives the reader an emotional reason to keep a journal. The copy then describes how it can be used and gives practical details such as size and binding. The product title and body use terms such as “hardcover poetry journal” and “gift for a writer” in context.

seo.title: Almost, Always | Mollie Sambrook
seo.description: Published product copy for a poetry journal designed around the words we almost say.

sample.objective: Set expectations for what subscribers will receive and give them a clear reason to sign up.

extracts.label: From the public sign-up
extracts.text:
A little correspondence from our corner of the literary world.

Original poetry, essays, reading recommendations and occasional glimpses behind the pages. Delivered to your inbox when there's something worth sharing.

sample.notes: The invitation and “SEND ME A NOTE” button frame subscribing as correspondence. The Mailchimp sign-up was configured. This sample contains the public acquisition copy. The welcome email text and its send status are unverified.

writing.title: Lessons in Anatomy
writing.description: An original poem adapted into an illustrated film and a literary art print.

image.alt: Rose-toned jellyfish from the finished film against dark water

sample.publication: Cold Feet Editions film and poetry print
sample.audience: Readers of contemporary poetry and viewers discovering the studio through illustrated short films.
sample.objective: Build an intimate observation around the sea, letting the natural world give shape to questions about suffering and memory.

extracts.label: Opening lines
extracts.text:
You sit your jaw on the horizon haze,
look at where boats
float over deep water

sample.notes: The film holds on the horizon before descending beneath the surface. The jellyfish gives the poem’s question about immortality a visual form. The adaptation extends the studio’s original writing into film and print.

writing.title: A Whole Lungful of Nostalgia
writing.description: An original poem about memory, distance and home, set into a literary print with a steam train illustration.

image.alt: Framed original poem with handwritten notes and a steam train illustration

sample.publication: The Things We Carry, Cold Feet Editions
sample.audience: Poetry readers drawn to work about place, memory and relationships.
sample.objective: Capture the intimacy of leaving a place through specific memories and ordinary details.

extracts.label: From the original poetry print
extracts.text:
Head on my shoulder, fold up beds,
holding my hands between yours like a promise,
blowing warmth back into my fingers.
Breathing warmth back into my heart.

sample.notes: The print pairs memories of being close to someone with the image of a departing steam train. Its handwritten lines and drifting smoke carry the sense of departure into the artwork.
